title: Rüeblitorte (Swiss carrot cake)
summary: A light, nutty Swiss sponge made mostly of ground almonds and grated carrot, lifted by whisked egg whites and finished with a thin lemon glaze.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C (350 °F). Grease a 24 cm (9½ in) springform pan and line the base with parchment.
Beat the egg yolks with the erythritol for 3–4 minutes until thick and pale. Beat in the lemon zest, lemon juice and kirsch.
Mix the almond flour, baking powder, cinnamon and salt, then stir them and the grated carrot into the yolk mixture. It will be stiff.
In a clean bowl whisk the egg whites to firm, glossy peaks. Stir a quarter into the batter to loosen it, then fold in the rest in two additions, keeping as much air as you can.
Scrape into the pan and bake 40–45 minutes, until risen, golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cover loosely with foil if it browns too fast.
Cool in the pan 10 minutes, release the side and cool completely.
Stir the powdered erythritol with the lemon juice to a thick, pourable glaze and spread it over the top. Let it set before slicing.
tips: The cake keeps and improves for 2–3 days, well wrapped; the carrot keeps it moist.
Leave out the kirsch for children or swap it for a few drops of almond extract.

origin.history: Rüebli is the Swiss German word for carrot, and the almond-and-carrot Rüeblitorte is closely associated with the canton of Aargau, sometimes called the Rüeblikanton. Made with ground nuts and little or no flour, it is a traditional birthday and Easter cake across German-speaking Switzerland, often decorated with small marzipan carrots.
